details.label: Discussion
details.text: Vigorous thunderstorm development, now in a linear band northeast of the Muncie through Lafayette vicinities, still appears rooted above a relatively stable boundary layer, along a weak low-level frontal zone. However, latest objective analysis suggests that low-level moistening along this boundary, coupled with perhaps subtle steepening of lapse rates aloft, have contributed to ongoing destabilization in a corridor ahead of activity through southwestern Ohio. Updraft inflow emanating from this environment might provide continuing support for strong thunderstorm development into the 13-15Z time frame, with some further organization possible aided by modest vertical shear. However, with lower- to mid-tropospheric mean westerly wind fields generally on the order of 20-25 kt, the extent of the potential for damaging wind gusts to increase remains unclear due to the lingering presence of weak low-level lapse rates

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...55-70 MPH · MOST PROBABLE PEAK HAIL SIZE...UP TO 1.25 IN
